quiz.q: On which three subjects did states first accede?
quiz.why: The Instrument of Accession covered defence, external affairs and communications.

quiz.q: What came after accession, in the video?
options: Integration: mergers, unions and centrally run areas
quiz.why: Accession came first; integration through mergers and unions followed.

quiz.q: Which union was inaugurated on 1 July 1949?
options: Patiala and East Punjab States Union
quiz.why: The White Paper gives 1 July 1949 for Travancore-Cochin; Saurashtra was February 1948.

episodes.title: How Language Redrew the States
sources: Wikipedia, 'Potti Sreeramulu', 'Andhra State', 'States Reorganisation Commission', 'States Reorganisation Act, 1956' (read 2026-11-18); SRC Report (1955)

quiz.q: Which state was created first, on 1 October 1953, on a linguistic basis?
quiz.why: Andhra State was formed from 11 Telugu districts of Madras State, with Kurnool as capital.

quiz.q: Who were the three members of the States Reorganisation Commission?
quiz.why: Justice Fazl Ali, K. M. Panikkar and H. N. Kunzru submitted the report in September 1955.

quiz.q: What did the States Reorganisation Act of 1956 divide India into?
quiz.why: The commission suggested 16 states and 3 areas; the Act made 14 states and 6 union territories.

quiz.q: What did the Convention declare on 21 September 1792?

quiz.q: Where does the Declaration say sovereignty resides?

quiz.q: What did the Calico Act of 1720 ban in England?
quiz.why: NCERT: a 1720 law banned the use of printed cotton textiles (chintz) in England.

quiz.q: By the 1880s, what share of cotton clothes worn by Indians was made in Britain?
quiz.why: By the 1880s two-thirds of cotton clothes worn by Indians were made of cloth produced in Britain.

quiz.q: Where was India's first cotton mill set up, in 1854?
quiz.why: The first cotton mill, a spinning mill, opened in Bombay in 1854.

episodes.title: Japan Changes Course: The Meiji Years

quiz.q: In which year did nationwide conscription begin in Meiji Japan?
quiz.why: The government instituted nationwide conscription in 1873: every male served four years from age 21.

quiz.q: Which model did the Meiji Constitution of 1889 follow?
quiz.why: It provided a constitutional monarchy based on the Prusso-German model.

quiz.q: What did Japan's 1905 victory over Russia do for anti-colonial nationalists?
quiz.why: It increased self-confidence among anti-colonial nationalists in colonised Asia, Indians included.

review.note: Facts were read against the Wikipedia pages listed (queue named NCERT world-history texts; not checked against them). Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

quiz.q: Which was the first census to be taken at the same time everywhere?
quiz.why: The 1881 census was the first synchronous decennial census.

quiz.q: Under which Act were all censuses since 1951 conducted?
quiz.why: All censuses since 1951 were conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

quiz.q: What was collected for the first time in the 2011 census?
quiz.why: 2011 marked the first time biometric information was collected.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a condition for a census town?
quiz.why: A census town is not statutorily notified as a town; it meets the three population, work and density tests.

quiz.q: By about how many times did India's urban population grow from 1901 to 2011?
quiz.why: From 25.85 million to 377.11 million.

quiz.q: Which factor is a 'push' towards cities?
quiz.why: High input costs and low income push farmers out of farming.

quiz.q: Which sea separated India from Asia before the collision?
quiz.why: NCERT: the Tethys Sea separated India from the Asian continent.

quiz.q: Roughly when did India collide with Asia, raising the Himalaya?
quiz.why: NCERT: India collided with Asia about 40-50 million years ago, causing rapid uplift.

quiz.q: What did the outpouring of lava about 60 million years ago form?
quiz.why: NCERT: lava outpouring and formation of the Deccan Traps started around 60 million years ago.
